items.text: AJ Vaccines is committed to ensuring that its employees have a safe working environment.

The National Authority of Polio-Containment conducted a 10-day GAPIV certification audit assessing AJ Vaccines' Biorisk Management System regarding legislative compliance related to handling and containment of polio virus.
AJ Vaccines has identified its main environmental impact to be release of infectious substances, energy consumption and noise emissions.
AJ Vaccines' environmental management system is anchored and headed by the department for Environment, Health and Safety.
AJ Vaccines provides relevant training and protective equipment to all employees.
AJ Vaccines encourages and supports a proactive approach to prevent and mitigate accidents and incidents related to safety risks.

In 2024, AJ Vaccines succeeded in demonstrating it is a responsible manufacturer by reducing the environmental impact of its business activities through implementing optimizations of manufacturing processes resulting in significant improvements of yields.
We aim to reach net-zero emissions across Scopes 1, 2, and 3 by 2050.
The current targets for Scope 1 and 2 emissions involve a 42% absolute reduction by 2030, using 2023 as the base year.

The target is for 70% of suppliers by spend, covering purchased goods and services and capital goods, and 90% of suppliers by spend covering upstream transportation and distribution, to establish science-based targets by 2029.
In 2024 we committed to a near-term science-based target to reduce GHG emissions in line with a 1.5°C global warming pathway.
The company aligns with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi).
The company aims to secure third-party validation for its emissions targets.
We intend to pursue SBTi validation of our near-term targets in 2026.
These are gross targets, with no reliance on GHG removals, carbon credits, or avoided emissions.
For Scope 3 emissions, we have committed to working with suppliers to align their practices with our climate goals.
We have committed to renewable energy sourcing, including a PPA for our Danish manufacturing site and Renewable Energy Credits for our Martinsried site.

We have committed to a transition from fossil fuel derived diesel to bio-based alternative at our Danish manufacturing site, and will investigate opportunities for other sites, which would reduce approximately 2.5 kg CO2e per liter compared to conventional diesel.
In 2024, the company began to assess the compatibility of its GHG emission reduction targets with a 1.5°C pathway.
Electrifying core operational systems to replace fossil fuel-dependent processes would reduce Scope 1 CO2e emissions by 73% compared to the 2023 baseline.
The company has a transition plan to reach climate neutrality by 2050.
The company has GHG emission reduction targets.
